record.paper_title: Completeness of sets of complex exponentials in convex sets: open problems
record.original_question: Let Λ = {λ_n} be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 not in Λ and λ_n tending to infinity, and let Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)}. For X equal to one of the intervals (-a,a) with 0 < a ≤ +∞, [0,+∞), or (-∞,0], with H(X) the space of continuous complex-valued functions on X that are holomorphic in the interior and carry the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets, which sequences Λ make Exp Λ complete in H(X)?

evidence.quote: Let Λ = {λ_n}, n ∈ N, be a sequence of pairwise different complex numbers (points) in the complex plane C, 0 ∉ Λ, and λ_n → ∞ as n → +∞. Let X be a convex open or closed set on C. By H(X) denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on X which are holomorpic in the interior Int X of X (if Int X ≠ ∅) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. An exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)} is complete in X if the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) coincides with H(X).
(2-!) In this case the completeness problem was solved completely by the profound Beurling-Malliavin theorem on the radius of completeness [1].

artifact.status_search_result: The completeness problem for exponential systems on symmetric open intervals (and equivalently on half-lines via standard reductions) was solved completely by the Beurling–Malliavin theorem on the radius of completeness (1962), which characterizes the completeness radius of Λ in terms of the upper Beurling–Malliavin density of Λ. This is widely recognized as a classical solved result.

status_evidence.title: Beurling–Malliavin theorem
status_evidence.snippet: The Beurling–Malliavin theorem gives the radius of completeness of an exponential system {exp(iλ_n t)} in L^2(−a,a), characterized via the Beurling–Malliavin density of Λ.
status_evidence.claim: The completeness problem for exponential systems on symmetric intervals is solved by the Beurling–Malliavin theorem.
